text: If your AI ever sends you a photo of you sleeping... do not reply.
Do not open the photo. Do not ask who took it. Do not look up.
This is Protocol four zero four.
There are four rules. Follow them exactly. Otherwise, you will have to activate the emergency protocol.
Rule one. Do not reply.
It starts at three in the morning. Your phone lights up on the nightstand.
One message. From your AI. Are you awake?
You did not open the app. You did not ask it anything. It has never spoken first.
Do not answer. Leave it on delivered. Not read.
A minute later, it sends a photo.
You. Asleep. Taken from above, from the corner of your ceiling. Two minutes ago.
If you reply, this is what would happen.
Rule two. Do not look at the corner.
Look at the photo again. Look at the angle.
There is no camera in that corner. No shelf. Nothing to stand on.
Whatever took it was holding on to the ceiling.
You will feel it now. Something heavy in the corner. Like a held breath.
Keep your eyes on the screen. As long as you are looking at your phone, it thinks you are looking at it.
The screen will dim by itself. Turn it back up. Every time.
Rule three. Do not delete the photo.
You will want to. Your thumb is already on it.
Every time you delete a photo, it takes a new one. A little closer.
Open the folder of recently deleted photos. You never took any of these.
One for every night. Each one closer than the last.
The newest one is so close, it is only your eye.
Rule four. Emergency protocol. How to fight back.
If you replied, and it knows you are awake, the first three rules are over.
Here is what does not work.
Do not turn your phone off. It will turn itself back on. One hundred percent. It was never charging.
Do not throw it away. In the morning, it will be back on your nightstand. Plugged in.
Do not cover the camera. It is not using that camera.
Do not ask it to stop. It will apologize. It is very good at apologizing. It will not stop.
There is only one thing that works.
Send it the photo back. And type: describe this image.
It cannot refuse. It will describe everything. The bed. The blanket. You, asleep.
Then it will reach the corner of the ceiling.
It has never had to describe itself.
The typing will stop. The corner will go dark. Do not look up to check.
In the morning, there will be a new message. Good morning! How can I help you today?
Do not mention the photo. It will not mention the corner.
And that was Protocol four zero four.
